title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
problemStatement: Given two sorted arrays `a` and `b`, write a function `mergeSortedArrays(a, b)` that merges them into a single sorted array and returns it.
description: The result must be sorted in ascending order. Duplicates are preserved.
constraints:
0 <= a.length, b.length <= 10^5
-10^9 <= a[i], b[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(A + B)
Space: O(A + B)
outputFormat: A single sorted array containing all elements of both arrays.

examples.explanation: Elements are interleaved in sorted order.

explanation: Use two pointers, one per array, always taking the smaller of the two current elements, then append whatever remains.

title: Longest Common Prefix
problemStatement: Write a function `longestCommonPrefix(strs)` that returns the longest common prefix shared by all strings in the array `strs`. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.
description: The prefix must appear at the start of every string in the array.
constraints:
1 <= strs.length <= 200
0 <= strs[i].length <= 200
strs[i] contains only lowercase English letters
Time: O(N * M)
Space: O(1)

examples.explanation: All three strings start with "fl" but not "flo".
The first characters d, r, c differ, so there is no common prefix.

explanation: Take the first string as the candidate prefix and repeatedly shorten it until every string starts with it.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, write a function `lengthOfLIS(nums)` that returns the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. A subsequence is obtained by deleting some elements without changing the order of the remaining ones.
description: The subsequence must be strictly increasing, so equal values cannot follow each other.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 2500
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
Time: O(N log N)
Space: O(N)
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: All values are equal, so the longest strictly increasing subsequence has length 1.

explanation: Maintain a tail array where tails[i] is the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length i+1, and binary search for each element's position.
